headline.affordTitle: What you can afford to test
headline.testBudgetEcom: Test budget (Option A: optimize for Purchase)
headline.optionBDesc: your budget is below Option A, so optimize for Add to Cart in week 1, then switch to Purchase. Keep cost per add to cart under about {cost} (an estimate).
headline.scaleTitle: If the test works: monthly budget to reach your target
headline.scaleTitleFixed: Your monthly budget after the test
headline.unreachable: Your target is above what the selected platforms can deliver. Google Search is capped by search volume, so add Meta or lower the target.

deliver.title: What it delivers
deliver.intro_leads: Monthly leads and how many turn into clients, based on your funnel rates.
deliver.intro_ecommerce: Monthly store visits, carts, purchases and revenue at this budget.

costs.title: Costs and verdict
costs.googleMaxHint: Up to about {spend} a month on Google Search
costs.tip_leads: CPL is ad spend ÷ leads. On its own it can mislead: a cheap lead that never books costs more per client.
costs.tip_ecommerce: CPA is ad spend ÷ purchases. Compare it with your break-even CPA.
costs.tip_cac: CAC is ad spend ÷ new clients. This is the number to compare platforms on for lead generation.
costs.tip_roas: ROAS is revenue ÷ ad spend. For lead generation, revenue is clients × client value.
costs.tip_google: Google Search can only show for searches that exist. This is the most results Google can deliver at your expected impression share.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.desc_profitable: Your expected cost is inside your target with a safety buffer. Scale in small steps and watch the cost.
verdict.desc_optimize: You can break even, but the margin is thin. Improve creatives, offer or funnel before scaling.
verdict.desc_notViable: Expected costs are above what you can afford. Fix the offer, price or funnel before spending more.

split.title: Budget split
split.intro: How the monthly budget is divided, and why.
split.chartLabel: Donut chart of the monthly budget split. The table next to it lists every amount.

reasons.prospecting: Finds new customers. Gets whatever is left after testing and retargeting.
reasons.creativeTesting: Gives each new creative enough spend to prove itself.
reasons.retargeting: Sized to show your recent visitors and engagers your ads about 8 times a month.
reasons.retargetingAudience: Sized to show your recent visitors and engagers your ads about 8 times a month.
reasons.retargetingCapped: Capped at the retargeting share of the Meta budget.
reasons.retargetingNewAccount: New account: add retargeting after 2 to 4 weeks, once there is an audience.
reasons.retargetingAudienceSmall: The retargeting audience is too small to deliver well yet.
reasons.retargetingOff: Retargeting is switched off in Planning.
reasons.brand: Protects searches for your own brand name.
reasons.noBrandSearches: No brand searches yet, so no brand campaign.
reasons.nonBrand: Captures people searching for what you sell.

platformReasons.lowestMarginal: Each extra step of budget went to the platform with the lowest cost for the next result.
platformReasons.googleCeiling: Google reached its ceiling: more budget would not find more searches at the same cost.
platformReasons.concentrated: The budget cannot cover the minimum for every platform, so it all goes to the one with the lowest expected cost.
platformReasons.belowMinimum: Its share was below its own minimum to learn, so it moved to the other platform.
platformReasons.searchIntentFirst: Lead generation: Google Search first (people already searching), up to its useful maximum.
platformReasons.metaFirst: Ecommerce: Meta first, as it creates demand at scale.
platformReasons.googleSmallShare: A smaller share for searches that already show buying intent.
platformReasons.remainder: Gets the rest of the budget.

split.adSets: Recommended Meta ad sets for this budget: {count}.
split.rampIntro: Raise the daily budget in steps so the learning phase does not reset.

bottleneck.title: Bottleneck finder
bottleneck.intro: What happens if each funnel stage improves by 10 percentage points.
bottleneck.saved: Saves about {amount} a month for the same clients

health.title: Account health
health.intro: Your current Meta numbers against common healthy ranges.
health.tip_cpm: Cost per 1,000 impressions. It depends heavily on country and season, so we show it for reference.
health.tip_ctr: Link clicks ÷ impressions. Below about 0.6% usually means the creative is not stopping the scroll.
health.tip_cvr: Results ÷ link clicks. A low rate points at the landing page or the offer.
health.tip_frequency: Impressions ÷ reach. Above 5 the audience may be tired of your ads.

scaling.title: Scaling table
scaling.limit: Profitable up to about {amount} a month. Above that, cost per result passes break-even.
scaling.noLimit: Within the range shown, cost per result stays under break-even.
scaling.chartLabel: Line chart of cost per result as the monthly budget grows, with the break-even line. The table below lists every point.

decision.title: Decision rules after the test
decision.intro: Compare the real cost per result from your test with these lines.
decision.scale: Switch to 'Has previous data' and plan the scale budget.
decision.optimize: Improve creatives, audience or landing page, then test again.
decision.stop: Fix the offer, price or funnel before spending more.
decision.stopLoss: Stop-loss: pause any ad set or creative that spends {low} to {high} with no results.
decision.biggestAssumption: Biggest assumption: {field}. It has the least reliable source, so check it first.
decision.creativeCheck: Creative testing needs about {amount} in total.

codes.multiCountry: You have data for {countries} countries. Costs differ by country, so a blended number can mislead. Check each country row.
codes.lowConfidence: {platform} has only {results} results in this period, so the cost is less certain. We blended it with a benchmark where one was available.
codes.missingData: {platform} is selected but has no usable data, so it is left out of the plan.
codes.seasonality: The planning month usually has different costs (multiplier {multiplier}). Budgets include this.
codes.targetUnreachable: The target cannot be reached with the selected platforms.
codes.creativeExceedsTest: Testing all your creatives costs more than the test budget. Test fewer creatives at once.
codes.optionB: Your budget is below Option A. Start by optimizing for Add to Cart, then switch to Purchase.
codes.testClientsFew: The test should bring about {clients} clients. That is usually too few to confirm your close rate, so keep tracking after the test.
codes.learningLimited: The budget is below what one ad set needs to exit learning. Use 1 ad set with a broad audience. Learning limited is acceptable if cost per result stays on target.
codes.optimizeATC: For ecommerce, consider optimizing for Add to Cart until purchases pick up.
codes.tooManyAdSets: You run {current} ad sets, but this budget supports about {supported}. Consolidate so each gets enough results.
codes.googleMinConversions: Google would get about {perCampaign} conversions a month per campaign, under the {min} smart bidding usually needs. Use fewer campaigns or a simpler bid strategy.
codes.googleCeiling: Google Search is at its ceiling of about {ceiling} a month. More budget there would mostly raise costs.
codes.splitConcentrated: The budget is too small to run every platform well, so it is focused on one.
codes.doubleCounting: Meta and Google may both claim the same sale or lead. Use your CRM or store as the source of truth.
codes.frequencyHigh: Frequency is {frequency}. Refresh creatives or widen the audience.

actions.pdfNote: Results are estimates, not guarantees. Real costs depend on your ads, offer, market and platform changes.

calc.title: How we calculated this
calc.intro: Each step shows the formula, then the same formula with your numbers.

profitPerClient.title: Profit from one new client
profitPerClient.desc: What you keep from a new client before paying for ads.

leadToClient.title: Share of leads that become clients
leadToClient.desc: How many leads make it through booking, showing up and buying.

maxCAC.title: Most you can pay for a client
maxCAC.desc: Paying more than your profit per client means losing money on every client.

targetCAC.title: Target cost per client
targetCAC.desc: We keep a safety buffer below the maximum.

maxCPL.title: What you can afford per lead
maxCPL.desc: Only some leads become clients, so each lead is worth a share of the client.

targetCPL.title: Target cost per lead
targetCPL.desc: The cost per lead that keeps your safety buffer.

profitPerOrder.title: Profit from one order
profitPerOrder.desc: What is left from an order after product, shipping, fees and returns.

breakEvenCPA.title: Break-even cost per sale
breakEvenCPA.desc: Spend more than this per sale and the order loses money.

breakEvenCPALifetime.title: Break-even cost per customer (lifetime)
breakEvenCPALifetime.desc: Judging on lifetime value lets you pay for repeat orders up front.

breakEvenROAS.title: Break-even ROAS
breakEvenROAS.desc: The return on ad spend where you neither win nor lose.

targetCPA.title: Target cost per sale
targetCPA.desc: We keep a safety buffer below break-even.

actualCPL.title: Your current cost per lead
actualCPL.desc: What leads actually cost in the period you entered.

actualCPA.title: Your current cost per sale
actualCPA.desc: What sales actually cost in the period you entered.

cpm.title: Cost per 1,000 impressions (CPM)
cpm.desc: How expensive it is to reach people in your market.

ctr.title: Click-through rate (CTR)
ctr.desc: How often people click your ads.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.desc: How many times the average person saw your ads.

monthlyBaseSpend.title: Current monthly spend
monthlyBaseSpend.desc: Your spend scaled to a full month. Costs start rising above this level.

workingCPA.title: Cost per result we plan with
workingCPA.desc: With few results, we blend your cost with a benchmark so one lucky week does not decide the plan.

workingCPANoBenchmark.title: Cost per result we plan with
workingCPANoBenchmark.desc: We use your actual cost. Below the minimum results it is less certain.

googleExtraImpressions.title: Searches you missed because of budget
googleExtraImpressions.desc: Impression share lost to budget shows how many more searches you could show on.

googleExtraSpend.title: Extra spend Google can absorb
googleExtraSpend.desc: What those missed searches would cost at your current click rate and price.

googleCeiling.title: Google Search ceiling
googleCeiling.desc: Above this, budget mostly buys more expensive clicks, not more searches.

estimatedCPL.title: Estimated cost per lead
estimatedCPL.desc: From the cost to reach people, how many click and how many of those become leads.

estimatedCPLForm.title: Estimated cost per lead
estimatedCPLForm.desc: From the cost to reach people, how many click and how many complete the instant form.

estimatedCPA.title: Estimated cost per sale
estimatedCPA.desc: From the cost to reach people, how many click and how many of those buy.

expectedCost.title: Expected cost for a new account
expectedCost.desc: New accounts usually pay more at first, and some months cost more than others.

costRange.title: Cautious end of the cost range
costRange.desc: Less reliable sources get a wider range. The result shows the high end.

googleImpressions.title: Searches you can show on
googleImpressions.desc: Monthly searches times the share you expect to win.

googleMaxClicks.title: Most clicks Google can give you
googleMaxClicks.desc: Impressions times the expected click rate.

googleMaxResults.title: Most results from Google Search
googleMaxResults.desc: Search volume limits Google. This is the most you can expect from it.

googleAvgCPC.title: Expected cost per click
googleAvgCPC.desc: The middle of Keyword Planner's top of page bid range.

googleMaxSpend.title: Most useful Google spend
googleMaxSpend.desc: Spending more than this cannot buy more searches.

googleExpectedCPA.title: Expected Google cost per result
googleExpectedCPA.desc: Cost per click divided by conversion rate, plus the new account penalty.

requiredLeads.title: Leads needed for your target
requiredLeads.desc: Only some leads become clients, so you need more leads than clients.

budgetForTarget.title: Budget for your target
budgetForTarget.desc: Costs rise as spend grows, so we search for the budget that still delivers enough results.

resultsForBudget.title: Results from your budget
resultsForBudget.desc: Costs rise as spend grows, so results grow a little slower than budget.

projectedCPA.title: Cost per result at this budget
projectedCPA.desc: Each doubling of spend above your current level raises the cost a little.

testBudgetLeads.title: Test budget
testBudgetLeads.desc: Enough for about 50 leads at the most you can pay per lead, so the test can exit learning.

testBudgetOptionA.title: Test budget (Option A)
testBudgetOptionA.desc: Enough for about 50 sales at break-even, so the test can exit learning.

testDaily.title: Daily test budget
testDaily.desc: The test budget spread across the test days.

creativeCheck.title: Creative testing cost
creativeCheck.desc: Each creative needs some spend to prove itself.

scaleThreshold.title: Scale line
scaleThreshold.desc: If the real cost comes in at or below this, scale.

testClients.title: Clients from the test
testClients.desc: Usually too few to confirm your close rate.

learningPerAdSet.title: Results per ad set per week
learningPerAdSet.desc: Meta needs about 50 a week per ad set to exit learning.

learningFloor.title: Monthly budget for one ad set to exit learning
learningFloor.desc: Below this, one ad set stays in learning. That can still be fine if costs stay on target.

supportedAdSets.title: Ad sets this budget supports
supportedAdSets.desc: How many ad sets can each get enough results.
